    What do you need from this run?

    Your answer picks the pathway: the modules the run will use, in order. Then choose how much you want to be asked. Every level runs the same modules by the same method; a level only changes which questions you answer and which take their defaults.

    How much do you want to be asked?

    Saved with the run, so Run activity shows who started it. Optional.

    Modules and turns

    By default every module of the pathway runs. A module you leave out does not run, and the modules a chosen module depends on are added.

    Modules to run

    A whole number from 1 to 64. The default is 32.

    A run cannot be corrected once it starts

    If the context changes, every module runs again: a resumed run refuses changed context. The cheapest fix is the right pathway now.

    Which documents does the issuer have?

    Pick the issuer's folder, or add files. Each file goes to the start service, which reads it as the run will (offline, no model) and lists what it recognises. The questions that follow are limited by what these documents support.

    Choose folder Add files

    Who is the issuer, and as of when?

    Each module's answer must name the issuer, one of its other names or its ID. Source readiness stops the run when it cannot tell whose files these are. The as-of date is the day the analysis stands on: evidence published after it counts as not yet available.

    The name the filings use for the group.

    Filled from the name: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, at most 40 characters. Use the same ID for every run on this issuer; the library files runs by it.

    One per line: the legal name if it differs, a short name, the ticker.

    Issue classification

    By the debt this run analyses; for split-rated or unrated issuers, use your firm's convention.

    Market situation

    Filled from the newest period end the documents state; correct it if a document is newer. Only checks the as-of date; not saved.

    On or after the newest file's date. Quotes, ratings, deal terms and peer figures dated after it are refused.

    The latest reported period, as the filing labels it: q1-2026 to q4-2026, h1-2026, h2-2026 or fy-2025.

    Earlier than the current period, and the same kind (quarter, half or year).

    As the filing cover states it: three uppercase letters.

    Items the research module reads that were published after it are refused. Follows the as-of date until you change it; set it earlier to leave out later research.

    Which file is the governing agreement?

    An agreement is something you point to, not something you declare. Choose the uploaded file that is the credit agreement or indenture, or say there is none. The service's reading of that file is kept: where you and the reading disagree, the run is told so and the disagreement is listed as a limit.

    The uploaded files. A 10-K or 10-Q that lists the agreement in its exhibit index is not the agreement.

    Summary and start

    This is the run you are about to start, as the launcher itself forecasts it from your documents and answers. It uses the paid model (USD 20 cap). Pages of the documents you uploaded that modules read are sent to OpenAI, and, unless the case is synthetic, the research module's web searches go to OpenAI's search: it is told to search with public names only, and the queries it actually sent are kept in the run record. For a private case the issuer's name and the questions it researches go to that search. Read it, accept each limit, approve, then submit once. Any change to an answer or a document needs a new summary.
